target: lead coordination time no more than 80 percent of a sequential baseline for the same lane count

subagent_arm.coordination_model: Lead authored two disjoint lane packets once, dispatched both lane subagents in a SINGLE parallel message, performed zero mid-flight interventions (no stalls, no out-of-scope edits to correct), then ran one git-based scope verification and read two return packets.
subagent_arm.lead_intervention_detail: 1 dispatch action; 0 mid-flight corrections; 1 post-run verification.

sequential_baseline.definition: Lead runs the same two lanes one after another (dispatch lane A, wait, collect, context-switch, dispatch lane B, wait, collect), each with its own framing and verification pass.
sequential_baseline.basis: Sum of the two measured lane durations (170537 + 249030 ms) plus a second full dispatch+collect+verify cycle the parallel approach avoids.

parallel_vs_sequential.result: PASS — parallel coordination measured at roughly 60 percent of the sequential baseline, within the <=80 percent target. Caveat: this measures the SUBAGENT parallel path, not the Terminal agent-team path; the team arm adds team-spawn and teammate-message overhead that must be measured separately before any team-specific labor claim.

team_arm.how_to_capture: In the Terminal team session, note wall-clock from team-spawn to both lane tasks closed, and count lead interventions (messages to teammates, nudges, stall recoveries). Record into team-arm-kit/evidence-template/coordinator-labor.json.
team_arm.warning: Known v2.1.177 team limitations (task-status lag, slow shutdown, no teammate resume) may RAISE coordinator labor vs the subagent baseline; that is exactly what the comparison must reveal.
